children: The gap between equity earnings yields and government bond yields has narrowed across major developed markets as bond yields have risen, with the compression particularly pronounced in the U.S., according to Liz Ann Sonders.
Sonders noted on X that the narrowing spread is “not a phenomenon unique to U.S.,” with a similar pattern visible across other developed markets.
The chart, based on S&P Dow Jones Indices data, showed the spread between forward earnings yields and 7-10 year government bond yields across the U.S., Canada, Japan, Australia, and the U.K.

The U.S. spread has narrowed sharply from around 2.7%-2.9% in mid-2022 to slightly below zero as of Aug. 31, 2026, according to the chart. The U.K. and Australia have also seen their spreads decline materially over the same period.

Japan continues to have the widest spread among the markets shown, although it has also narrowed, moving from around 7% in early 2023 toward 6% by late 2023 and standing near 3.3% as of Aug. 31, 2026.
Canada's spread stands at around 2.0%, while the U.K. is near 2.5% and Australia is close to 0.3%, based on the chart's latest readings.
Sonders said the U.S. spread may be tighter than those in other markets but emphasized that the broader compression is visible across developed markets.

title: Bond yields squeeze equity risk premium across developed markets
